items.stimulus: A musicologist studying 18th-century military bands measures the inside of a cylinder-shaped snare drum held in a regimental collection. The interior has a diameter of 20 inches and a height of 8 inches.
items.stem: What is the volume, in cubic inches, of the interior of the drum?
items.explanation: The volume of a cylinder is $V = \pi r^2 h$. The diameter is 20 inches, so you halve it first to get a radius of $r = 10$. Then $V = \pi(10)^2(8) = \pi(100)(8) = 800\pi$ cubic inches.

A.why: You used the radius but didn't square it. You calculated $\pi(10)(8) = 80\pi$ when you needed $\pi(10)^2(8)$.

B.why: You calculated $\pi d h = \pi(20)(8) = 160\pi$. That's the area of the drum's curved side, not the space inside it.

D.why: You used the diameter of 20 as the radius, so you got $\pi(20)^2(8) = 3{,}200\pi$. That's 4 times too big. Halve the diameter before you substitute.
